text: Azure Blob Storage is genuinely one of the most common landing zones for raw data in a real Data Factory pipeline — cheap, enormously scalable, and readable by nearly every other Azure service. It's also a genuinely representative example: once you've built one linked service by hand, the pattern barely changes from connector to connector.
The exact same starting point as any connector at all. Open the Manage hub, select Linked services, and select New — Lesson 6's general pattern, applied here for real.
Search for blob, and select the Azure Blob Storage connector from the gallery. Hundreds of connectors, narrowed down to one single search term.

Configure the connection details, test the connection, and select Create. Name it something meaningful, pick an authentication method, point it at a real storage account, and always test before you actually save it.

This particular connector supports six real authentication methods, more than most. Account key is simple, but grants full access to the entire storage account. Shared access signature is scoped and time-limited, genuinely safer. Service principal authenticates as an app, a solid choice for unattended pipelines. And managed identity needs no stored credential at all — for anything beyond a personal learning environment, that's genuinely the right default.

Testing the connection catches real problems immediately — a typo in the account name, a blocking firewall rule — before you've built a single dataset or pipeline on top of a connection that was never going to work in the first place. Next: connecting to Azure SQL and on-premises SQL Server, and the gateway that actually bridges the two.
